craft_notes: Sthāyin: the cross-examination (what could a means do? nothing — four times). Sanskrit: na svarūpalābho...na jñaptiḥ...nāvaraṇavigamaḥ...na tadanupraveśaḥ → L4 keeps the na-frame as 'It can't' ×4. Essence 2 (four-impossibilities→means-void). Close: no outsider to go in (the fourth impossibility — distance itself impossible — as landing). Rejected: varying the four closings for elegance — killed: the Sanskrit varies the grounds (nityatvāt/svayaṃprakāśamānatvāt/asaṃbhavāt/abhāvāt) while holding the na-frame; L4 mirrors: holds 'It can't', varies the ground; 'self-shining' for line 4 — killed: you-shine-already sings and carries svayaṃprakāśamānatvāt without the mouthful. Read aloud: four hammer-falls, each landing on the ground-word (eternally / already / none / go-in).

lines: Here "yoga-limb" means one thing only: thinking it through.
But what is there to think? The Lord, who is self-shining, is yourself.
So what could a means do? It can't get you your nature — you have it eternally.
It can't inform you — you shine already.
It can't strip a covering — there is none.
It can't take you inside — there's no outsider to go in.
l4.sanskrit_cite: atra ca tarka eva yogāṅgam iti kathaṃ vivecayati iti cet ucyate yo 'yaṃ parameśvaraḥ svaprakāśarūpaḥ svātmā tatra kim upāyena kriyate na svarūpalābho nityatvāt na jñaptiḥ svayaṃprakāśamānatvāt nāvaraṇavigamaḥ āvaraṇasya kasyacid api asaṃbhavāt na tadanupraveśaḥ anupraveṣṭuḥ vyatiriktasya abhāvāt

reads_against.argmap: What can means accomplish? → Every use of means is void: nothing to attain, notify, unveil, or enter — all is Śiva already.
c1_essence: Four impossibilities: no nature to attain, nothing to notify, no covering to remove, no one to enter; the means itself impossible.
